name: Kimi-K3-Nota-Global-Pruned-25
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (config.json max_position_embeddings 1048576). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated MLA on 24 layers + Kimi Delta Attention on 69 layers, with Attention Residuals
license: other (kimi-k3 licence; card sets license_name: kimi-k3)
notes: ADDED 2026-11-01. A non-uniform GLOBAL expert pruning of moonshotai/Kimi-K3, not a merge, not a quant and not a config-preserving edit: 61,824 routed experts remain across the 92 MoE layers (379 to 896 per layer, versus a uniform 896 in the base), total 2.099T against the base's 2.780T, i.e. 25% of experts removed. The per-layer counts ship in config.json as n_routed_experts_per_layer and stock vLLM sizes every layer from a single scalar num_experts, so the repo also patches the vLLM modeling file - it will not serve in unpatched vLLM. Deployment drops from 8x B300 to 6x. Recorded because the card prints base / REAP-25% / this-model columns in one table with a stated config (thinking on, max_tokens 32768): IFEval 93.72 -> 94.45, GPQA-Diamond 86.36 -> 87.37, IFBench 70.75 -> 70.75 (exact tie), HumanEval+ 82.32 -> 82.93. Read this as PARITY at 25% fewer experts, not as a capability gain: the two 'wins' are +0.73 and +1.01pp, and the card itself documents up to 1.22pp run-to-run movement on HumanEval+. The one clear win over the method it is benchmarked against is GPQA-D (87.37 vs REAP's 82.83), where REAP collapses and this does not. The 50%-pruned sibling is already in the catalog as a demo...
